title: Cohomology properties of maps in (Cat) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Problem served (continuing p.(2)): for a basic localizer W on Cat (Grothendieck's 'W-asphericity' axiomatics), show that certain squares of small categories are W-homotopy cocartesian. The intended application (p.3) is that for presheaves on A, a pushout Y'=Y'⊔_Y X with Y→X a monomorphism is sent by i_A = A/(-) : Â → Cat to a homotopy pushout. Consequently W-equivalences of presheaves that are monos are stable under pushout.

The setup. Take a cartesian square of small categories, Y = Y'×_{X'} X, with maps i:Y→X, g:Y→Y', f:X→X', i':Y'→X'. Assume f and i' are cofibrations, meaning cofibred functors (opfibrations). Assume that for each object x' of X', one of the fibres f^{-1}(x') or i'^{-1}(x') is trivial; see the corrections below. Write ∫(i,g) for the Grothendieck construction of the span Y' ←g– Y –i→ X. This is the categorical double mapping cylinder, a model of the homotopy pushout. Consider the canonical functor p: ∫(i,g) → X'.

Theorem. Under these hypotheses p is a cofibration. Its fibre over x' is the Grothendieck construction of the span of fibres Y'_{x'} ← Y_{x'} = Y'_{x'}×X_{x'} → X_{x'}, with the two projections as maps.
- If Y'_{x'} = e, the fibre is ∫(e ← A = A).
- If X_{x'} = e, the fibre is ∫(A = A → e).
- In the degenerate case, where i'-fibre is empty and f-fibre is e, the fibre is e.

Each such fibre is the cone C(A) glued to the cylinder A×Δ^1 along A, i.e. C(A) ⊔_A (A×Δ^1). The cylinder deformation-retracts onto its end, so the fibre deformation-retracts onto the cone C(A). The cone has a terminal (or initial) object, hence is W-aspherical ('on gagne!').

By the localizer axioms (a cofibred functor with W-aspherical fibres is W-aspherical, hence in W), p ∈ W.

Corollary. If i ∈ W then i' ∈ W; if g ∈ W then f ∈ W. The proof uses:
- homotopy invariance of ∫ for spans: a pointwise W-map of spans gives a W-map on ∫;
- ∫(Y = Y → Y') ≃ Y' (cylinder retraction);
- 2-out-of-3 applied to Y' → ∫(i,g) → X'.
So the square is W-homotopy cocartesian.

The cut-off 'Lemme si ∫(Y→X, ↓Y') ... (f^{-1})' probably begins a statement about fibres. The margin note 'remplacer avec fibrations' prepares the dual version. That dual is the one needed on p.3: A/Y → A/X etc. are discrete fibrations, and A/Y' → A/X' is a fibrant mono, i.e. an open immersion (sieve). Its fibres are therefore e or ∅. Over a point of Y' the f-fibre is the discrete set Y_{y'}; off Y' it is e. So the hypothesis is satisfied.
errors: The condition as transcribed ('f^{-1}(x') ou i'^{-1}(x') soit vide') cannot be right. It would force Y = Y'×_{X'}X to be empty, and it contradicts the stated fibre forms ∫(A→A, ↓e) and ∫(A→e, ↓A). The intended condition is that one of the two fibres is reduced to a point e. In the application, the i'-fibre is a point or empty, and when it is empty the f-fibre is a point.
'Commutatif' is written above 'cartésien'. Cartesianness is genuinely needed to identify Y_{x'} with Y'_{x'}×X_{x'}.
Cofibrancy of ∫(i,g)→X' also uses that f∘i = i'∘g is a cofibration. This holds since a base change and composite of cofibrations is a cofibration, but it is not stated.

Passing to the corollary silently uses homotopy invariance of the Grothendieck construction of spans and 2-out-of-3. These are standard consequences of the localizer axioms, but they are not spelled out.

For the fibration (dual) version needed on p.3, the cone has an initial rather than terminal object. It is still aspherical by the axioms, via a natural transformation to a constant functor, but the dualisation is only flagged in the margin.

ideas.what: Grothendieck construction of a span as the categorical homotopy pushout (double mapping cylinder), with its comparison functor to X'
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck construction / homotopy colimit of a span in Cat (Thomason)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 VI (construction); used throughout Pursuing Stacks

ideas.what: Criterion: a cartesian square of cofibred functors, with one of the two fibres trivial over each object, is homotopy cocartesian for every basic localizer W. Proof: ∫(span)→X' is cofibred with fibres deformation-retracting to cones.
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy cocartesianness of pushouts along sieves/cosieves in Cat for any fundamental localizer
ideas.usually_credited_to: D.-C. Cisinski (thesis 2002; 'Le localisateur fondamental minimal' 2004; Astérisque 308, 2006)
ideas.where_published: Possibly sketched in Pursuing Stacks discussions of model structures on Â; this exact formulation unsure

ideas.what: Corollary: W-equivalences are stable under these pushouts. Applied on the next page to show that W-equivalences of presheaves that are monomorphisms are stable under pushout (the key step towards a model structure on Â).
ideas.modern_name: Left properness / stability of trivial cofibrations under pushout in Cisinski's model structure on presheaves
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks raises the model-category question for Â; proof details unsure

ideas.what: Fibre ∫(e←A=A) ≅ C(A)⊔_A(A×Δ^1) deformation-retracts to the cone, hence is aspherical

missed.claim: Grothendieck has a complete short proof, valid for an arbitrary basic localizer, that cartesian squares of cofibred functors with point-or-empty fibre conditions (e.g. pushouts along open immersions, images of presheaf pushouts along monos) are homotopy cocartesian. He then deduces stability of W under such pushouts. In the literature this is attributed to Cisinski's later work, since these Montpellier notes were inaccessible.
missed.quote: Ce foncteur est une cofibration, à fibres les ∫(Y_{x'} = Y'_{x'}×X_{x'} → X_{x'}, ↓Y'_{x'}) ... donc asphériques ... Corollaire i ∈ W ⇒ i' ∈ W, g ∈ W ⇒ f ∈ W
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority for a key step in the theory of fundamental localizers and Cisinski model structures. The fibrewise argument via the Grothendieck construction is also a clean, axiom-only proof.

deep.surprise_reason: A correct, finished proof of a key lemma later established by Cisinski. The method is natural and the result well known today; its interest is mainly priority and documentation.
transcription_corrections: 'soit vide' should read as a statement that the fibre is a point (≅ e, 'ponctuel'), not empty; the handwriting is unclear but 'vide' is mathematically inconsistent.
The interpolation '{+au lieu de il : la catégorie pré-cartésienne [?], et considérons+}' is better read as 'au lieu de il : la catégorie [...], et considérons le foncteur canonique'.
The margin reads 'remplacer avec fibrations' (dual version for p.3), plus 'suffit de vérifier...'.
The boxed passage should read roughly: 'La catégorie ∫(A→A, ↓e) est C(A) ⊔_A (A×Δ^1) ... C(A) est un rétracte par déformation, on gagne!' (the cone is a deformation retract).
